identity.title: Huxley-G\"odel Machine: Human-Level Coding Agent Development by an Approximation of the Optimal Self-Improving Machine

problem.claim: Develop self-improving coding agents that search trees of self-modifications.

gap.claim: Benchmark performance can mismatch an agent’s potential for further self-improvement, termed the Metaproductivity-Performance Mismatch.

contributions.claim: Proposes CMP, which aggregates descendants’ benchmark performances as an indicator of self-improvement potential.
Reports that access to true CMP is sufficient to simulate Gödel Machine behavior in the stated setting under certain assumptions.
Introduces Huxley-Gödel Machine, which estimates CMP to guide self-modification-tree search.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish their approach by guiding self-modification search with an estimated descendant-performance aggregate rather than relying only on current benchmark performance.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that HGM outperforms prior self-improving coding-agent development methods on SWE-bench Verified and Polyglot while using fewer allocated CPU hours.
The authors report strong transfer to other coding datasets and LLMs.

The authors report human-level performance when an agent optimized on SWE-bench Verified with GPT-5 mini is evaluated on SWE-bench Lite with GPT-5, matching the best officially checked human-engineered-agent results.

narrative_sequence.summary: Self-improvement is operationalized through agents that edit their own codebases.
Methods expand modification trees by favoring higher coding-benchmark performance as a proxy for promising future modifications.
The paper identifies a mismatch between benchmark performance and metaproductivity.
It proposes CMP and HGM, using estimated descendant performance to guide tree search.
HGM is reported to outperform prior methods with fewer CPU hours, transfer across datasets and LLMs, and reach the stated human-level result.

source_observation.claim: The abstract explicitly separates current coding-benchmark performance from self-improvement potential and introduces a descendant-based metric to represent the latter.

lessons.interpretation: When a proxy may conflate present capability with future improvement capacity, modeling downstream performance can sharpen search guidance.
lessons.application: Define and evaluate a proxy based on descendants or later-stage outcomes when selecting among iterative system improvements.
lessons.exception: This move may be unsuitable when descendants are too costly to generate or when downstream performance is unavailable or unreliable.

unknowns: The assumptions required for the Gödel Machine simulation are not specified.
The abstract does not give CMP’s exact aggregation formula, benchmark scores, CPU-hour counts, baselines, or statistical details.
The transfer claim does not specify which datasets or LLMs were used.
